articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 4 days away from their 2026 NFL season opener, and here’s a look at which players wore No. 4 best.
articles.body:
Fans only need to wait 4 more days until the Steel City brand of football returns when the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Atlanta Falcons on September 13. In the spirit of the countdown to kickoff, we'll take a look at the most recent and best players ever to wear No. 4.

Metcalf, who was traded to the Steelers in March 2025, is the current No. 4 wearer on the roster.

Steelers training camp: Early photos of action in Latrobe

Best No. 4 in Steelers history: P Josh Miller

No. 4 doesn't have the same historic weight as other Steelers' jersey numbers, but the best wearer is punter Josh Miller.

Miller, who signed with Pittsburgh in 1996, became one of the most reliable punters in Steelers history the late 1990s and early 2000s. During his Steelers tenure, Miller punted 572 times for 24,547 yards, the second most in franchise history.

After leaving Pittsburgh, Miller went on to win Super Bowl XXXIX with the New England Patriots, but his longer run with the Steelers makes him deserving of being named the greatest to ever wear No. 4.

articles.title: Coco Gauff comes back to beat Mirra Andreeva, heads to US Open semis
articles.summary: Coco Gauff beats Mirra Andreeva in US Open quarterfinals. She will next play No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina in the semifinals.
articles.body:
NEW YORK - Coco Gauff saved two match points in the second set and came back to beat French Open champion Mirra Andreeva 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-2 in another thrilling US Open quarterfinal match at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Gauff, the No. 3 seed, will face No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina in one semifinal on Sept. 10. Top seed Aryna Sabalenka will face third-seeded Jessica Pegula in the other semifinal.

Andreeva won the first seven points of the match, and most of Gauff's mistakes were her own doing.

Gauff, who has won 11 matches in a row, struggled with her serve, which was broken on her first two serves, leaving her down 4-0 within 12 minutes, and Andreeva finished off the set against the 2023 US Open champion in 26 minutes. The roles were reversed in that final set, as Andreeva melted down, especially in her last service game, where she committed four unforced errors, all of the forehand variety.

Another forehand volley error ended Andreeva's time in New York, as the victorious Gauff dropped her racket and threw her hands in the air and screamed in jubilation.

The second set was more of the same for Gauff; even though she got out to a 5-3 lead and was serving for the set, she committed three of her 12 double faults in the game, allowing Andreeva to seize momentum.

But just like the previous five quarterfinal matches on Arthur Ashe, this one went the distance.

The second-set tiebreak featured a 39-shot rally, giving Gauff the slightest edge, but another unforced error by Gauff was nullified when she saved two match points, the last when Andreeva's return off a Gauff forehand went weakly into the net, finally ending the 80-minute set.

After Andreeva was broken in the third set, frustration started to mount as she bounced her racket on the court while walking to her bench. All four of Andreeva's US Open career losses have come against Americans, including a loss to Gauff on her way to the 2023 title.

articles.title: Opponent Offense Preview: Utah State Aggies
articles.summary: The struggling Broncos come to Husky Stadium.
articles.body:
The Aggies are 0-1 after a stunning 29-17 loss to FCS Idaho State . They are coached by a familiar name in Bronco Mendenhall, who has faced the Huskies as coach of BYU three times, winning just once. The Washington defense largely played a great game last week and should be feeling confident against an Utah State offense that's stuck in the mud. To the preview.

(Small sample size alert: they've played one game)

QB McCae Hillstead is a name Aggie fans know well. He started as a true freshman at the school back in 2023 before transferring to BYU for two seasons, then came back to Logan this offseason and won the job outright in April. He's got some mobility (nine carries for 43 yards in the opener) and reportedly impressed his new coordinator in the spring with how much of the complex playbook he could handle. But his first game this season was rough, going 15-of-30 for 178 yards and two touchdowns against FCS Idaho State, including two late interceptions when his team was down, which made it three total picks on the day. They were all very poor throws and reads. He's the type of player almost better when the play breaks down and he can improv a little bit. If he struggles against UW, keep an eye on graduate senior Grady Brosterhous, who saw time late after Hillstead threw his third interception (5-of-13, 67 yards, a pick, plus 10 carries for 35 yards). Brosterhous also comes in for designed runs from time to time.

At running back, graduate senior Javen Jacobs is arguably their best player and probably the safest bet on this offense. He led the team with 80 yards on 20 carries in week 1 and also caught four passes for 27 yards. Last season, he had 65 carries and 47 receptions, as well as returned punts and kick offs, so he's a do-it-all workhorse. Sophomore Noah White, who played as a true freshman last year, is behind him (though he had just three carries week 1).

The receiver room is almost entirely new, but a couple of guys flashed early. Graduate senior Eli Wood is a former walk-on from UVA and led the team with six catches for 90 yards and a score, and can make some nice contested catches. Graduate transfer Demick Starling added three catches for 30 yards and the touchdown that briefly put Utah State ahead in the third quarter. Junior Rex Haynes is a 6-5 option and started strong with a 23 yard catch in the opening play of the game (though he was left basically uncovered.) Lastly, senior Javon Robinson is the speedy playmaker (relatively) and they look for him on screens. He had three catches.

The one thing the offensive line can hang their hat on is continuity, as three of Utah State's four returning offensive starters from a year ago are on the line, led by senior left guard George Maile, who started all 13 games there a year ago. With basically everything else turned over, this group is supposed to be the steadying influence. That being said, they gave up 3 sacks and 6 TFLs to Idaho State. Not terrible numbers, but it's concerning from the experienced part of your offense against an FCS team.

Utah State handed the keys to OC Robert Anae this offseason after losing their previous play caller to Utah. Anae comes with some pedigree, especially under Mendenhall, with 15 years working together. They built a top-10 rushing attack at BYU, and a 2021 Virginia offense that finished third nationally in total yards per game while setting a school record for passing yards. His teams have finished top 25 nationally in an offensive statistical category 56 times over his career (per the schools press release when they hired him in January of this year).

The system is built on quick passing, power running, and a lot of pre-snap motion and formation shifts to put stress on a defense's eyes. They also showed some "slow mesh" against Idaho State, where the QB and running back have a long, exaggerated hand off to read the defense before deciding which one takes the ball. If I were a Utah State coach, I would see all the young players in Washington's front seven and do everything to confuse them about where the ball is going. Aggie players on the roster have called it different from anything they've practiced against before. In theory it should be an adaptable attack, but week 1 showed the growing pains of installing a new system with such a new roster.

Utah State actually won the numbers against Idaho State, but just played losing football. They had more total yards, more than double the first downs (29 to 14), and nearly seven more minutes of possession, yet still lost by 12 points, mostly because of four turnovers. If Washington's front is half as active in this game as they were against Washington State , Utah State will likely cough up the ball multiple times and be unable to finish drives. They lack the explosive playmakers needed to consistently beat this defense.

If the Huskies can rattle Hillstead the way Idaho State did (likely), particularly on early downs, this offense shouldn't find much success. The key will be not flushing him from the pocket into open space where he can use his mobility, but rather keeping him in the pocket and forcing him to throw downfield — or better yet — sacking him outright. I don't think Washington's defense needs to be dominant here, it just needs to not allow mistakes and penalties to keep give Utah State momentum and confidence.

articles.title: Chaz Lanier May Not Survive Pistons’ Training Camp
articles.summary: The Pistons' offseason rumor mill has been focused on Jalen Duren, but there's also chatter that Chaz Lanier is in a tough spot. It's not hard to see why. Go...
articles.body:
The Pistons' offseason rumor mill has been focused on Jalen Duren , but there's also chatter that Chaz Lanier is in a tough spot. It's not hard to see why.

Going into his second season in Detroit, the young star has somewhat managed to distinguish himself as a reliable three-point option. But after a busy offseason, the Pistons are loaded with more capable, experienced, and versatile distance shooters. If he can't find his spot in the rotation quickly, Lanier might find himself looking for a new team in the next few weeks.

Detroit took Lanier 37th overall in the 2025 draft. They signed him to a four-year contract worth over $8.6 million, with a team option for the fourth year. Lanier spent a chunk of his rookie season in the G League, playing 18 games with the Motor City Cruise. The problem for him is that he played only 34 games on the main roster and didn't exactly blow anyone's mind.

Lanier played roughly 7.7 minutes per game with the Pistons, averaging 2.4 points, 0.7 rebounds, 0.5 assists, and 0.2 steals in each appearance. Those aren't the kind of numbers that make a big impression on coaches and the front office. Again, it was his rookie season, so the team has to give him a bit of leeway. Now, Lanier is going into his second season and needs to start making waves if he wants to hang around on this roster. The Pistons are in the process of making some big decisions after all.

The biggest storm Detroit is dealing with is the Duren situation . There is a real possibility that it doesn't get sorted out before the season starts, destroying his relationship with the franchise and turning him into an unrestricted free agent in 2027. Going into training camp for 2026-2027, that means the Pistons are throwing every player under the microscope to see how they fit, including Lanier.

Over the course of the 2026 offseason, Detroit gained the services of Isaiah Joe , Taurean Prince , and Gary Harris , all of whom are lethal from distance. The front office also re-signed Kevin Huerter , which was a bit of a surprise . That doesn't mean he isn't also dangerous shooting from three. On top of that, the Pistons still have Duncan Robinson , one of the best in the business, as well as Cade Cunningham , who is a threat from anywhere on the court every time the ball is in his hands.

The reality is that the Pistons have a roster loaded with absolute sharpshooters. Detroit's current projected depth chart lists Robinson as its starting shooting guard, with Joe as his backup. Heurter, Harris, and Daniss Jenkins are listed as the Pistons' reserves. Lanier, who is a shooting guard, doesn't appear in that projection at any position, let alone shooting guard.

Detroit's depth at the two is quite impressive and could improve. The Pistons have made it clear they are focused on developing Jenkins, which could leave someone like Lanier out in the cold. Anyone the coaches or front office think isn't pulling their weight will find themselves on the trading block rather quickly. That's assuming they make it through training camp, which could be a legitimate concern for Lanier.

Training Camp Could Make or Break Lanier

As it stands, Lanier's contract has guaranteed money through the end of the 2026-2027 season. The last two years of that contract are not guaranteed. If the Pistons aren't impressed by what they see from Lanier in training camp, they could waive him and only have to pay out this season's salary of $2.15 million. That's not exactly a huge amount of money in NBA terms.

This wouldn't free up cap space for the Pistons right now, but it would help in the future. Keep in mind that Detroit is currently over the cap but well under the luxury tax going into this season. As such, they're not likely to replace him. Even stretching his guaranteed salary across a couple of seasons won't do much for them. Adding players isn't the goal here. The Pistons' roster is fine for the offseason, but they have too many players for the regular season. Cuts will need to be made during training camp, and Lanier is a likely target.

For him, it's a bad combination of not having a unique skill set on this roster and a contract that's easy to waive, stretch, or absorb. Unless Lanier shows up in a big way during training camp and proves himself to be a building block for the future, it would not be a surprise to see his name in a press release from the Pistons about his departure before the season starts.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy starts international stretch with title defense at Irish Open
articles.summary: McIlroy reflects on what the Irish Open means to him; vies for repeat victory and Race to Dubai record.
articles.body:
Two hundred sixty miles from where he first learned the game, across the border of the Republic of Ireland, down south on the Clare Coast, Rory McIlroy is teeing it up at his national open in Doonbeg. It's a homecoming, in a way, for McIlroy, though the last time he'd been to this part of the Emerald Isle was "over 20 years ago."

McIlroy is from Holywood, Northern Ireland. For a man on a golf odyssey who has been everywhere, won everything, and is known by everyone, this island is where he feels at home.

McIlroy has won the Amgen Irish Open twice, in 2016 and 2025, both at the K Club. Last year was an emotional win for the Ulsterman, as he sunk a dramatic, 28-foot eagle putt to force a playoff with Joakim Lagergren, whom he eventually bested on the third hole of sudden-death. Coming only months after he completed the elusive career Grand Slam, McIlroy described winning his home country's open in retrospect on Wednesday as a "magical weekend" and "very fulfilling."

His home Open means so much to him that he has gone as far as lobbying for its champion to receive a Masters invite, saying Wednesday that he "spoke to [Augusta National] Chairman Ridley about this a lot. … I think, hopefully, at some point, it's inevitable that that would become a reality."

McIlroy has always been a global player, but remarked that in recent years he's redoubled his efforts to "really focus on this part of the season."

This year, he vies for his fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title, and also attempts to equal Colin Montgomerie's all-time record of eight.

McIlroy described this tournament stretch of the Irish Open, the BMW PGA at Wentworth (only miles from where he now lives,) the Middle East swing, and the Australian Open, as "very meaningful to me."

As for the current state of his game, McIlroy's trending in the right direction, coming off a T-4 in his last start at the Tour Championship after struggling at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

"I played Memphis and played very poorly, and was looking at my swing on video and just didn't like where it was," he said.

In the aftermath, he decided to make swing changes, explaining: "not changes that are unfamiliar to me. Changes that I've had to do before."

As McIlroy returns to his homeland this week hoping to lift the trophy again, it's the perfect time and place for those familiar changes to take shape.

articles.title: Gauff beats Andreeva to reach US Open semifinals in comeback win
articles.summary: Coco Gauff sets up US Open semifinal with Elena Rybakina after saving two match points against Mirra Andreeva.
articles.body:
American Coco Gauff saved two match points to beat Russian fifth seed ⁠Mirra Andreeva 2-6, 7-6 (7), ⁠6-2 on Wednesday and reach the US Open semi-finals after recovering from a dreadful opening set.

The 2023 champion had none of her usual firepower at first and was ⁠on the ropes in the tiebreak before she flipped the script and closed out the match with a forehand strike, dropping her racket to the court in joy and relief.

She faces second seed ⁠Elena Rybakina in the semi-finals.

“The motto of the match was just to fight,” said Gauff.

Andreeva looked completely at home in New York City’s Arthur Ashe Stadium as she sprinted through the first four games, never allowing Gauff to set up a break-point chance in the opening set where the Russian had just five unforced errors to ‌14 from her opponent.

Gauff, who took a break in the locker room between sets, took inspiration from her compatriot Frances Tiafoe, who recovered from two sets and a breakdown on Tuesday night to reach the semi-finals on the men’s side.

“I just had to reset. I came out not feeling the ball, giving her too many free points,” said Gauff. “I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe and how he came back yesterday. And we all want to do well in front ⁠of this crowd.”

Gauff finally found some momentum in the second set and ⁠was serving for the match in the ninth game when old issues with her serve resurfaced. She produced three double faults, allowing her opponent to break back.

Undeterred, Gauff recovered her poise and deployed a perfectly placed backhand to win a 39-shot ⁠rally, twice saving match point before forcing the third set with a forehand shot to the corner that Andreeva could not contain.

She kept up ⁠the pace from there, and Andreeva flung her racket at her ⁠bench in disgust after dropping her serve in the third game of the decider. Gauff broke her to love in the seventh game to put the contest completely out of reach.

She faces a formidable foe in Rybakina, who claimed the top ranking ‌with a win earlier in the day over Zheng Qinwen of China.

Gauff and the Kazakh second seed have one win apiece in career head-to-head, with Rybakina winning their most recent encounter in the semi-finals in Toronto ‌last ‌month.

“Elena – she’s the new world number one so it’s going to be a tough match,” said Gauff. “I’m looking forward to the battle. These are the moments you live for.”

articles.title: English Open: Mark Selby defeats Zhang Anda to progress to third round
articles.summary: World number two Mark Selby progresses to the third round of the English Open by winning a deciding frame against China's Zhang Anda.
articles.body:
World number two Mark Selby progressed to the third round of the English Open by winning a deciding frame against China's Zhang Anda.

Selby completed a final clearance of 39 to win the final frame 59-49, taking victory on the black.

Zhang had levelled the tie at 3-3 with a century break, after Selby has turned round a 2-1 deficit to lead 3-2.

The 43-year-old will now meet Kyren Wilson, who won 4-3 against Wuhan Open champion Chang Bingyu, in the last 16 in Brentwood.

Oliver Lines, who defeated world number one Zhao Xintong in the first round, exited the competition with a 4-3 defeat to Yuan Sijun, losing the last two frames having pulled back from 2-0 down to lead 3-2.

World number three Judd Trump moved into the third round with a 4-1 win over Ashley Carty and will play Anthony McGill, who defeated Fan Zhengyi 4-1.

Barry Hawkins beat Daniel Wells 4-1 to set-up a tie with Mark Williams, who triumphed 4-3 over Matthew Selt, while Wu Yize sealed a 4-2 victory over compatriot Xu Si and will now face Liam Davies, who took a 4-1 win against Xinbo Wang.

Shaun Murphy and Ali Carter were the only 4-0 victors in the round, beating Jamie Clarke and Robbie Williams respectively.

articles.title: WWE's Liv Morgan Cast in Psychological Thriller 'Ping' After Role in 'Bad Lieutenant' Movie
articles.summary: WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan will be starring in the upcoming psychological thriller, Ping, per a report from Deadline's Andreas Wiseman.
articles.body:
WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan will be starring in the upcoming psychological thriller, Ping , per a report from Deadline's Andreas Wiseman .

This will be Morgan's third film. She previously appeared in the 2023 movie, The Kill Room .

Morgan is one of the top billings in the upcoming movie, Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo , which will premier at the Toronto International Film Festival on Monday.

Ping is currently under production in Mississippi, per Wiseman. The film stars Megan Lawless, who recently had a major role in the massive hit, Obsession as Sarah Harper. As relayed by Deadline, the film is about "an aspiring creative director lands a remote dream job" who is then "forced to choose between her sanity and a boss she can never mute."

Writer-director Richie Gordon had this to say on the movie as well, per Deadline .

" Ping examines the promises of modern work that can push us to work harder and longer, sometimes at the expense of ourselves – it asks those of us living through burnout culture: what is enough? I was blown away by how deeply that resonated with Megan and the rest of the cast, and am incredibly fortunate to have some of the best crew in the business to bring it to life. I'm in awe of the talent behind this film and I can't wait for the world to see it."

In the meantime, Morgan continues her third singles world championship reign. She most recently defeated Stephanie Vaquer at RAW on Monday thanks to interference from Judgment Day.

articles.title: Quinn Hughes Talks Potential Wild Contract Extension After Cale Makar's Historic Avalanche Deal
articles.summary: Quinn Hughes hasn't yet played a full season with the Minnesota Wild, and he isn't feeling much urgency to sign a new deal with the team.
articles.body:
Quinn Hughes hasn't yet played a full season with the Minnesota Wild, and he isn't feeling much urgency to sign a new deal with the team.

"This is going to be done whenever I feel like it needs to be done," Hughes, who has one year remaining on his contract after coming over to Minnesota from the Vancouver Canucks via trade last season, said Wednesday, per Dan Rosen of NHL.com.

"I don't feel backed up against a wall. I'm very thoughtful. I want to make sure I'm taking my time on everything and make sure I'm making a decision that is going to be good for everyone. That's kind of where my head has been at.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

"We haven't had that many conversations just because of how I wanted my summer to go in terms of being fresh and resetting and enjoying and training and being around friends and family. As we get going here I'm sure it'll heat up, but I don't feel backed up against a wall where I have to sign before camp."

There could be something of a blueprint in place.

Rosen noted the defenseman's next deal is expected to pay him roughly the same amount of money per year as Colorado Avalanche defender Cale Makar after the latter agreed to an eight-year, $163.2 million deal this sumer.

Makar set the NHL record at $20.4 million per year.

Hughes is just 26 years old and one of the best defensemen in the league, and it would be anything but a surprise if the Wild give him a deal worth more than that in an effort to keep him with the team beyond just the 2026-27 campaign.

While he isn't in a rush to sign at this point, he said he could "of course" see himself in Minnesota for the foreseeable future.

So is he worried about contract negotiations carrying into the season?

"It's not going to weigh over me personally," Hughes said. "I mean, I'm excited to play hockey. I think if I can stay healthy I'm going to have my best season. I feel great. So I don't have it weighing over me, I don't think."

Hughes' resume already includes two All-Star selections and the 2023-24 Norris Memorial Trophy as the league's top defenseman.

He helped lead the Wild to the second round of the playoffs last season and could be a franchise cornerstone moving forward. First, though, the two sides need to come to terms on a new deal.

articles.title: Dodgers Admit They Should’ve Handled Shohei Ohtani Injury Differently
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts voiced regret from the organization over their handling of Shohei Ohtani's injury.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts voiced regret from the organization over their handling of Shohei Ohtani's injury.

According to manager Dave Roberts, who spoke with the media, including Dodgers Nation, the team would love to go back and put Ohtani on the injured list, given he is already set to miss at least six of the last seven games, with more possibly in store.

The skipper said that Ohtani did not properly communicate the problem with his swing from the only game he has played in a week, Monday's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds .

Ohtani has missed six games out of the team's last seven, including Wednesday night's series finale against the Reds.

Once Ohtani entered the batting cages on Tuesday, he informed the team and staff about his discomfort.

"The concern is that after 4 days, to take 4 AB's and feel something, we can't keep going forward. That's disappointing," Roberts said.

Additionally, the big problem for the Dodgers would be that any injured list placement would be 15 days at minimum rather than 10 days.

"It's not ideal given that it would be 15 days. Whatever is best for him is best for us. We'll have to make that decision in time," Roberts added.

"It's his bicep, his arm. It's not one specific thing."

Unfortunately, Ohtani could be halfway through an IL stint already, with no game action in between that may have resulted in recovery.

Now, if he went on the IL, he may be looking at coming back on September 23rd at the earliest, leaving him a handful of games.

articles.body:
Since his injury and fall in production last season, Patrick Mahomes has faced more doubt than at any point in his tenure with the Kansas City Chiefs . However, veteran analyst Colin Cowherd may have taken it a step too far.

With left tackle Josh Simmons likely missing the Week 1 game against the Denver Broncos , there has been speculation about how it could affect the two-time MVP. But when the radio Hall of Famer picked Justin Herbert over him, fans were left aghast at the disrespect.

Fans Incensed About Colin Cowherd's Patrick Mahomes Comments

Returning from a torn ACL that had his status for Week 1 in question throughout the offseason has already been a miraculous turnaround for Mahomes. But coming into the game against a team that had 68 sacks last season without its starting left tackle complicates matters even further.

However, Cowherd took it a step too far on the latest episode of "The Herd." He tried to use the missing left tackle as an argument for Herbert over Mahomes, citing the Los Angeles Chargers ' injuries to the offensive line last season.

"When Justin Herbert is missing a left tackle, he makes the playoffs. When Mahomes doesn't have a left tackle, he doesn't," Cowherd claimed. "That's his kryptonite."

Unfortunately, fans found his take to be revisionist of the actual NFL history.

Matt Verderame of SI Now was stunned by the claim, arguing, "This has to be one of the most disingenuous things I've ever seen. Mahomes won three SBs with three different LTs, including spare parts all over the line around them. What are we doing? I feel like I don't cover the same sport as other people."

But rather than go back and cover the length and breadth of Mahomes' career to include all three Super Bowl victories, Chase Snyder pointed to the most recent time the Chiefs reached the Super Bowl.

"The Chiefs had four starting left tackles the year he went 15-1 and went to their third consecutive Super Bowl after winning back-to-back titles. What are we doing?" Snyder asked.

The claim felt so bizarre for those who had followed the Chiefs regularly that Joshua Brisco admitted to being "ashamed" to even acknowledge Cowherd's comments. He wrote, "This is obviously so factually incorrect that I'm almost ashamed to even acknowledge it."

Bleacher Report's Daniel Harms, too, was aghast at the comments from Cowherd, directly calling him out, "*checks the Chiefs LT history since the Eric Fisher days*. I suggest you check your facts on that one, Colin. Dumbest thing I've seen from this account in a while, which is saying something."

As one fan called his comments "bafflingly stupid," others referred to them as " very shameless."

All across social media, it was hard to find any defense for Cowherd's premise, given the history of Mahomes and his offensive line concerns.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

One fan pointed to the timeline of the last four years, where the three-time Super Bowl champion also lacked a true superstar wide receiver talent after the Chiefs traded away Tyreek Hill .

"He's had 10 different starting left tackles since 2022 and won 2 Super Bowls, along with 3 AFC Championships. Stop the nonsense, Colin!"

Rather than argue the facts, though, one fan turned sarcastic against the veteran analyst: "Yeah, watch me just make up a bunch of [expletive] when I could check the facts and see I'm completely wrong."

Others followed a similar train of thought as well, as one fan called out, "I honestly don't think @colincowherd watches any games, he just says dumb [expletive] for clicks."

According to PFN's Team OL Impact Metric , the Chiefs' offensive line posted an impact score of 74.1 last season, ranking 20th in the league.

It remains to be seen whether the comments from Cowherd line up with the post-injury version of Mahomes we are going to see this season. But before this year, it felt impossible to argue that the circumstances surrounding the roster had affected his ability to lead the team in any significant way.

articles.title: Star subs rescue Chelsea as Alonso 'takes blame'
articles.summary: Chelsea get the better of Leeds in a cup thriller, but Blues boss Xabi Alonso has food for thought after needing rescue act from his star substitutes.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso watched his Chelsea team hit six goals in the second half against Leeds United but felt the need to "take responsibility" for the shaky start that came before the thrilling flurry.

Amid jubilation that followed the final whistle at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea recovered from 2-0 down to progress as 6-3 winners in the Carabao Cup, it was easy to forget that Alonso's side were booed off at half-time.

Supporters witnessed arguably the worst first half of Alonso's short tenure to date, with Chelsea fortunate not to be further in arrears after the head coach made nine changes to his line-up.

The team's rhythm was disrupted. Leeds made eight changes themselves, but Daniel Farke's side took control and were threatening to surge into the fourth round.

Defender Tarik Muharemovic opened the scoring before Brenden Aaronson doubled Leeds' lead shortly after the break.

Alonso had responded to Chelsea's out-of-sorts start by making four substitutions at half-time. On came Cole Palmer , Morgan Rogers , Pedro Neto and Reece James , and together they changed the game.

The sight of Palmer and Rogers warming up had gladdened the hearts of many, turning jeers to cheers. By the end of the night, Palmer had scored twice, fellow substitute Neto had also found the net, and Rogers left the field after helping to create four goals from open play in Chelsea's remarkable turnaround.

However, speaking after the match, Alonso said he had made it "hard" for his players in the first place.

"I need to take my own blame and my own responsibility on the things that happen," he said. "I need to be able to help them better so they are not responsible, and after you need to react and think what's better for the team."

Alonso said the raft of substitutions he felt compelled to make should be considered "part of the game".

Stars keep hopes alive for fringe players

For the Premier League's biggest clubs, this competition is usually an opportunity to blood youngsters and give fringe players valuable minutes.

However, only 35-year-old Danny Welbeck , who scored twice, emerged from the starters with a compelling case for more regular involvement.

Even Valentin Barco, despite scoring Chelsea's fifth goal, was partly at fault for Leeds' second and was among several players who repeatedly surrendered possession during a difficult first half.

Young attackers Estevao Willian and Jamie Gittens suffered the disappointment of being substituted at half-time, while £40m signing Geovany Quenda , who joined from Sporting, did not add to his solitary substitute appearance for the club as he watched from the bench.

Midfielder Reggie Watson, making his debut at the age of 16, was also withdrawn at the break after being booked.

Alonso later said he would not take a "cynical" view as some on the outside might about the difference in level between his proven stars and Chelsea's back-up options.

He added: "I know that probably I have to take the right decisions for them to show their best level, so it's something that I will analyse and learn from today."

Nevertheless, reaching the fourth round is important for Chelsea.

It is not only about preserving their hopes of silverware in a season without European football, but Chelsea are also a club that need as many competitive fixtures as possible.

They have a 27-man squad, supported by a strong academy pipeline, and these matches are vital for keeping a large group of players engaged throughout the campaign.

There is an irony, then, that Palmer, Rogers and Chelsea's other established stars may have secured future opportunities for the very fringe players whose performances had put the club's EFL Cup campaign at risk.

articles.title: You Can Criticize Carson Hocevar, But You Can’t Ignore His Improvement.
articles.summary: There are plenty of things you can criticize about Carson Hocevar. His aggression has gotten him into trouble. He’s made mistakes, created controversy and co...
articles.body:
There are plenty of things you can criticize about Carson Hocevar.

His aggression has gotten him into trouble. He's made mistakes, created controversy and collected a growing list of drivers who probably aren't sending him a Christmas card.

But if the argument is that Hocevar doesn't have the performance to back up the confidence, that's where I disagree. Because the numbers tell a different story.

*Hocevar's 2026 and Blaney's 2018 statistics reflect the first 26 races of their respective third full-time Cup Series seasons.

Through the 2026 regular season, Hocevar earned his first Cup Series win, five top-five finishes, nine top 10s and two poles. Compare that to 2025, when he finished the entire season with two top fives, nine top 10s and one pole. In his 2024 rookie season, he had just one top five and six top 10s.

He's not just producing occasional flashes of speed, either. Hocevar led only 16 laps during his rookie season and 122 last year. He led 157 during the first 26 races of 2026 alone. His average starting position improved from 17.6 in 2025 to 12.2 this season, while his average finish improved by nearly five positions to 16.7.

For some perspective, Ryan Blaney was at a similar point in his third full-time Cup season. Through 26 races in 2018, Blaney had five top fives, 12 top 10s and two poles. Hocevar has five top fives, nine top 10s and two poles through the same number of races this season — with a win already on his resume.

The point isn't that Hocevar is following Blaney's exact trajectory. It's that expecting a 23-year-old in his third full-time Cup season to already perform like a finished product ignores how development at NASCAR's highest level can work.

And before his recent slump, the results were showing that development. Hocevar left Indianapolis fifth in the Cup standings and as the highest-ranked Chevrolet driver.

One top-20 finish across the final four regular-season races, three finishes of 31st or worse and two DNFs dropped him to 12th entering the Chase. His struggles continued at Darlington, adding more fuel to the conversation about his recent performance.

That stretch deserves criticism. But four or five bad races don't erase what came before them.

Hocevar still has plenty to clean up. The aggression that makes him exciting can also put him in situations that cost himself and others, and turning raw speed into consistent results remains an important part of his development. But that's a different argument than saying the performance isn't there.

You don't have to like how Carson Hocevar races. You don't have to like his personality, either. But the argument that the performance isn't there? The numbers are making that harder and harder to defend.

articles.title: Dodgers veteran gives team another injury-related headache to deal with down stretch
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani is not the only Dodgers star suddenly battling an injury. First baseman Freddie Freeman is dealing with a right knee issue, manager Dave Robert...
articles.body:
First baseman Freddie Freeman is dealing with a right knee issue, manager Dave Roberts said, which was severe enough to keep him out of the team's lineup for Wednesday's series finale against the Reds .

That marked the second time this homestand that Freeman was out of the Dodgers' lineup and came on the heels of a rare start for the veteran slugger as designated hitter on Tuesday.

Roberts said there was no specific incident that led to Freeman's knee problem, and that an injured list stint was not under consideration for the 36-year-old.

However, Roberts believes that Freeman's injury contributed to his recent 1-for-18 slump at the plate, one that has dropped his season batting average under .300 for the first time since late July.

"Freddie does a really good job of hitting against his front side [in his swing]," Roberts said. "So when you can't do that with your front side, your right knee, then you're compromised. And I see there's a lot more swing and miss the last few days; that's just not who he is."

Roberts didn't set a date for when Freeman would return to the Dodgers' lineup, wanting to exercise caution with the 10-time All-Star's workload over the stretch run of the regular season.

The manager left open the possibility of Freeman returning to action for the team's next game on Friday, when it begins a weeklong road trip starting in Miami .

But, "it's also a possibility that we give him three days off to then get back," Roberts said, "getting him ready optimally for the September run."

For now, it's just one more injury-related headache for the two-time defending champions to deal with.

articles.title: Michigan Hockey Accused of Years of Sexualized Hazing
articles.summary: Sixteen former Michigan hockey players have filed a federal lawsuit alleging severe sexualized hazing inside the program from 1984 through 2001.
articles.body:
According to an exclusive report from the Detroit Free Press , sixteen former University of Michigan hockey players have filed a federal lawsuit accusing the school of allowing years of severe, sexualized hazing inside one of college hockey's most prominent programs.

The lawsuit, filed Wednesday in federal court in Detroit, covers alleged conduct from 1984 through 2001. The plaintiffs are identified only as John Does and accuse older players of subjecting younger teammates to ritualized abuse that included forced nudity, forcible shaving, burning of pubic hair and other sexualized acts.

The University of Michigan and its Board of Regents are the only defendants. Former coaches Red Berenson and Mel Pearson are not named as defendants, but the complaint alleges coaches and staff knew about the conduct, tolerated it and in some cases pressured players to participate.

Michael Pitt, an attorney representing the former players, told the Detroit Free Press that his clients are seeking accountability while protecting their identities.

Lawsuit Alleges Hazing Became Part of Michigan Hockey Culture

The allegations go beyond claims that upperclassmen acted without supervision.

According to the complaint, players who resisted or complained were allegedly told they were not being good teammates or were challenged to "be a Michigan man." The lawsuit further alleges that participation became understood by younger players as a condition of remaining accepted within the program.

Some plaintiffs claim their playing time was reduced after objecting.

That distinction will be central to the case. Hazing carried out secretly by players presents one set of questions. The plaintiffs are alleging something considerably broader: that adults responsible for the program knew what was occurring and helped create an environment in which players believed refusing could carry consequences.

The complaint specifically alleges that practices continued during Berenson's tenure and also references Pearson, who later became Michigan's head coach.

None of those allegations has been proven in court.

Berenson Publicly Ended Freshman Hazing in 2012

One piece of Michigan hockey history takes on new relevance because of the lawsuit.

More than a decade after the period covered by the plaintiffs' allegations, Berenson publicly announced in 2012 that Michigan was eliminating freshman hazing from the program.

"We've taken all of the little freshmen things out of our program," Berenson said at the time . "It's hard enough to make the transition as a freshman without going through some of that. It's borderline embarrassment or humiliation."

The practices Berenson discussed publicly in 2012 were far less severe than those described in Wednesday's lawsuit. The reported freshman duties included carrying pucks, loading buses and going last through meal lines.

His comments do not establish what coaches knew about the conduct now alleged by the former players. They do establish that freshman hazing had long been recognized as part of the program's culture before Berenson formally ended what he publicly described.

Lawsuit Arrives During Another Michigan Athletics Transition

The timing creates another institutional problem for Michigan.

The athletic department is already undergoing leadership changes following an outside review and Warde Manuel's decision to leave the athletic director position at the end of 2026. The transition has included questions surrounding Manuel's departure agreement and the university's explanation of the athletics department review .

Michigan hockey has faced its own scrutiny before. Pearson was removed as head coach in 2022 following an investigation into the program's culture and other allegations of misconduct. The current lawsuit concerns a much earlier period and makes separate allegations, but it puts institutional oversight of the hockey program back under examination.

It also arrives after Michigan agreed in 2022 to a $490 million settlement with more than 1,000 people who accused former university physician Robert Anderson of sexual abuse.

Former Players Seek Damages and Policy Changes

The 16 plaintiffs are seeking an unspecified amount of monetary damages.

They are also asking the university to require sexualized-hazing prevention training for Michigan athletes, making the lawsuit about more than financial compensation.

Pitt said the university had known for more than a year that litigation was possible but had not reached a resolution with the former players.

The university, Board of Regents and hockey program had not provided the Free Press with a response to the allegations at the time the original report was published.

For Michigan, the next stage will move beyond describing what allegedly happened decades ago. The case will test whether the plaintiffs can establish their broader claim that the culture was known, protected and reinforced by people responsible for stopping it.

articles.title: Taylor Lapilus vs. Mitch McKee to crown bantamweight champion in last PFL event
articles.summary: PFL will transition to Most Valuable Promotions in 2027
articles.body:
PFL will crown its bantamweight champion on Dec. 19 in Lyon, France, when Taylor Lapilus faces off with Mitch McKee for the inaugural 135-pound belt in the main event of the last PFL card before merging with MVP in 2027, the promotion announced Wednesday.

Lapilus (25-4) won four in a row under the PFL banner after parting ways with the UFC on a two-fight winning streak, topping Jake Hadley in his most recent bout this past May. The 34-year-old French bantamweight was victorious in six of eight bouts over two stints in the UFC.

"My whole career has led to this moment," Lapilus stated in a release. "I'm here to become champion, leave my mark on this sport, and cement my legacy. And when I look back, I want to know I was part of the moment everything changed for French MMA. This is more than a title fight. This is history in the making."

McKee (11-0) is a decorated wrestler and undefeated MMA prospect who earned a shot at the PFL gold after beating former Bellator titleholder Sergio Pettis via decision in April, his first appearance under the company's banner after a successful 8-0 run in LFA.

"Fighting for a PFL world title is exactly why I came here," McKee said. "Taylor is a great fighter, he's experienced, and I know fighting him in France means I'm walking into his backyard. I wouldn't want it any other way. I've believed from day one that I'm the best bantamweight in the PFL, and in December I get the opportunity to prove it. I'm going to Lyon to bring that belt home."

The final four PFL shows before the transition under the MVP name are scheduled for Oct. 16 in Chicago, followed by a pair of November events before the last trip to Lyon.

"Lyon has become one of the great fight cities in the world, and the energy French fans bring for their athletes is palpable," MVP CEO John Martin stated in a release. "On December 19, fans will have the opportunity to see one of their own fight for a world championship as Taylor Lapilus takes on the biggest test of his career in the undefeated Mitch McKee. … The night will also mark a major milestone for our company as the final event under the PFL banner before we move forward as MVP in 2027. I can't think of a better city or a better stage for it."

articles.title: Marquette Women’s Soccer Preview: at #17 Baylor & vs Loyola Chicago
articles.summary: Off to Waco for a battle with a ranked opponent before coming home for a local-ish contest.
articles.body:
Marquette has a double whammy facing them as they go into a pair of matches this weekend.

No, it's not because they're facing a ranked Baylor team, clearly their toughest test of the season so far.

Whammy #1 is because this is Marquette's first match without leading scorer Megan Murray. She's off at the Asian Games with the Philippine national team for the month. She'll miss at least five matches, maybe more, depending precisely on when she returns to North America. Murray has three goals to lead Marquette so far this season, and she's also the only Golden Eagle with 10 or more shots through six matches. Murray's all the way up at 13 attempts, and that's after going without a shot against both Truman State (she only played 16 minute) and Wisconsin.

Whammy #2 is the fact that Murray hasn't scored since Marquette's second match of the season… and Marquette hasn't score at all as a team since Kaylie Sheehan found an equalizer in the 79th minute against Wisconsin. That's two straight matches without a goal and just over 200 minutes.

On one hand: Losing your top goal scorer is not good. On the other hand: She hasn't scored in four straight matches. On a secret third hand: No one has scored in either of the last two matches. How does Marquette adjust to defenses not paying attention to Murray, or is the fact that defenses now don't know who to look at to worry about the most actually helpful to the Golden Eagles' offensive issues?

Here's another question: How much pressure has Murray generated to this point of the season to help the Marquette defense? The Golden Eagles haven't allowed a non-penalty kick goal at all this season through six matches. That's outstanding work no matter how you slice it, and limiting opponents to less than nine shots per match is helping out a lot there. Is Murray's offensive work partially responsible for keeping the ball away from freshman keeper Mia Hurd? How will Marquette adjust without Murray and keep the offensive pressure up to keep doing Hurd a favor over the next month?

There's a lot going on here, and it's possible that we won't even learn anything useful on that topic from Thursday night just because of the quality of the opponent!

Date: Thursday, September 10, 2026 Time: 7pm Central Location: Betty Lou Mays Field, Waco, Texas Streaming: ESPN+ Live Stats: Stat Broadcast , in theory

This is the first ever meeting between Marquette and Baylor.

Baylor has been all over the place in the United Soccer Coaches poll this season. Receiving Votes, #6, Receiving Votes, and #22 last week before moving up to #17 now. Beating #10 Arkansas 4-1 to start the season went a long way towards grabbing attention, but so did losing 3-1 to Texas State at home 11 days later. It was just the kind of attention that you don't really want. They have won three in a row since then, toppling Texas, Pepperdine, and LSU to get to five wins on the season.

Eight different women have combined for their 14 goals to this point of the year. Lauren Omholt and Grace White are your leaders with three goals each. Omholt has to settle for a tie for the team lead in points, as Theresa McCullough has two goals and four assists to get to eight points as well. To give you an idea of what kind of style of play we'll see from the Bears, Baylor has 18 assists this season on their 14 goals, led by those four from McCullough. Nine different women have a helper already, and six of them have two.

Azul Alvarez is your keeper here, and things haven't been super great for her. She's stopping less than 70% of shots on goal, and that's after stopping all three attempts against LSU last time out. Thanks to giving up three goals in the Texas State match, Alvarez is letting in 1.17 goals per 90 minutes this season. If you wanted to lean towards "it's going to get better for her," that's a safe bet. Alvarez stopped 83% of shots while posting a goals-against average of 0.82 last season that earned her All-Big 12 First Team honors.

Match #8: vs Loyola Chicago Ramblers (2-2-2)

Date: Sunday, September 13, 2026 Time: 1pm Central Location: Valley Fields, Milwaukee, Wisconsin Streaming: ESPN+ Live Stats: Stat Broadcast

Marquette is 5-1-1 all time against Loyola Chicago. Three of the meetings were back in the 1990s, and then there was a 2005 and a 2008 out of nowhere. The rivalry popped back up in 2014 , and now this is the first time that the Golden Eagles and the Ramblers have faced off in consecutive seasons since the first two meetings. Last year's contest went to a 1-1 draw in the Valley .

Loyola's season has gone all over the place so far this season. 1-0 campaign opener home win over Central Michigan? Check. 5-0 loss on the road against an Iowa team that was earning top 25 votes? Check. Getting outshot 21-3 by #5 Michigan State in East Lansing but only giving up a goal in the 83rd minute for a 1-0 loss? Check. 2-0 home win over Illinois State? Check. Back-to-back scoreless draws against cross-town rivals Northwestern and DePaul? Check. As I write this preview ahead of both matches, the Ramblers have yet to score a goal in the month of September, although they do have to visit Northern Illinois on Thursday night, so we'll see.

There are just three total goals scored by Loyola this season, which makes Maggie Schmidt the most important offensive player on the team. She has two of the three goals, and Sarah Collins has the other. With that said, Josslyn Weissman is the leading shot taker on the roster. She has seven attempts to lead Loyola there, but as you can tell, none of them have gone into the net yet this season. Weissman had three goals for Manhattan last season, so we'll see how this all shakes out as an offensive plan against the Golden Eagles.

It looks like a pretty safe bet that we'll see Allison Deardorff patrolling the net in this one. The senior from Itasca, Illinois, has played every minute so far this season and is up to 28 saves already. She's stopping over 82% of shots on goal, which is a little bit propped up by 10 saves against Iowa and another eight against Northwestern, but the math is what the math is. The two scoreless draws the last time out have dropped her goals-against average down to an even 1.00 per 90 minutes right now.

articles.title: John Harbaugh pushes back on Giants media over Malik Nabers questions: ‘We can make it uncomfortable’
articles.summary: The New York Giants kick off the 2026 NFL season on Sunday night against the rival Dallas Cowboys. It’s the debut of first-year head coach John Harbaugh, and...
articles.body:
The New York Giants kick off the 2026 NFL season on Sunday night against the rival Dallas Cowboys . It's the debut of first-year head coach John Harbaugh, and you know he wants to make a good first impression for his new team.

On Wednesday, the former Baltimore Ravens coach met with the local media to discuss how things are going heading into the Sunday Night Football showdown, and a big question on everyone's mind was whether wide receiver Malik Nabers might play. Nabers, who hasn't played since tearing his right ACL last September, was a full participant in Wednesday's padded practice.

Harbaugh was naturally asked about Nabers during the presser, and he was initially upbeat about answering questions about the possibility of him playing.

"I think he's ready to go, man," he told reporters. "We'll see. It's still four days until we play. If he's ready to go, and he feels like he's ready to go, then he'll play. If he's not ready, then he won't play."

New York media members don't love wishy-washy, so they kept pressing Harbaugh for something more specific about the possibility that Nabers might play. And eventually, he snapped.

"I can just say this right now. We can put a stop to all these questions, because I'm not going to tell you who is playing in the game," said an animated Harbaugh. "I'm not going to tell you who is starting, I'm not gonna tell you what package we have in, I'm not gonna tell you which play we're running. I'm not going to tell you any of that. So we can make it great and have a great press conference, or we can make it uncomfortable. But I'm not going to tell you because when you know, the Cowboys know, or every other team we play knows. And that's not in the competitive interest of our football team. I think you can respect that."

That kind of thing might fly in Baltimore, but the New York media isn't likely to be too put off by Harbaugh's threat of an "uncomfortable" presser. In fact, the reporter who asked the offending question immediately followed up to say the question was still relevant, and the Giants coach seemed to agree, answering it fairly.

Much like in Baltimore, if the Giants win under Harbaugh, he won't have to worry about too many "uncomfortable" press conferences. But if they falter, he probably hasn't even seen "uncomfortable" yet.

articles.title: Temple DB could be looking for revenge against Penn State

Penn State will be renewing its longstanding series with the Temple Owls this weekend. The two teams have played each other 45 times altogether, but this will be their first meeting since 2016.

The Nittany Lions have won 39 of the last 41 games in the series, but their most recent loss came in 2015. It's important not to take Temple lightly after seeing just how close the two sides have played each other in the last couple decades. One of the players on their defense who could wreck the game is safety Kolin Dinkins .

Not only is he one of the best players on the Owls ' defense, but he also used to play for Penn State. Dinkins was mainly a special teamer during his time in State College, so he'll come in with something to prove against the school he didn't get many snaps at.

He had three tackles in Temple's first game against Rhode Island, which is nearly half the number of tackles he had all of last season. After having so much success on special teams in the past, we know Dinkins is an athletic defensive back who isn't afraid to get physical.

We saw the Nittany Lions struggle to get the run game working last weekend, so Dinkins' impact could be felt there. He has some of the best pedigree on the Owls' roster and some added motivation to have a big game. Matt Campbell and his staff need to make sure they keep their eyes on Dinkins and don't allow him to wreck the game.

articles.title: Oklahoma Sooners will be tested but too much for Bryce Underwood
articles.summary: Oklahoma Sooners defense will face a tough task with Bryce Underwood but they have the talent to shut down the former 5-Star prospect.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners have an opportunity in front of them when they go on the road to take on the Michigan Wolverines in Week 2. Sure, Michigan is coming off a dreadful offensive performance, but this team has the talent to create problems. Oklahoma won't overlook the Wolverines .

But the Sooners match up well with what Michigan wants to do. The Sooners also have the talent to disrupt Michigan's young quarterback, Bryce Underwood.

Underwood was a five-star prospect in the 2025 recruiting class and won the Michigan job as a true freshman. In year one, he completed 60.3% of his passes for 2,428 yards, 14 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions. He also ran for 392 yards and six touchdowns.

He's a quarterback that Oklahoma head coach Bryce Underwood has a lot of respect for.

"All of his best days are still in front of him," Venables said at his Tuesday news conference . "Won nine games as a starting quarterback, as a true freshman, a tremendous feat in itself. And we've got a great, great challenge."

Being the starting quarterback at the collegiate level takes some talent. Starting as a true freshman at the University of Michigan is even harder.

"He is in a completely different system this year than what he was a year ago," Venables said . "I don't ever look at it as a life of its own. This guy can run it, he can throw it, he's decisive at making decisions, and he's a rhythmic player. He's really good that way."

Underwood has all of the tools to be really good. He's had some nice moments in his Michigan career. Unfortunately, those positive moments are fewer against the better defenses.

In 2025, Underwood and the Wolverines played three games against teams ranked in the top 20 in scoring defense: Oklahoma, Washington, and Ohio State. Michigan went 1-2, earning a 24-7 win over Washington in a game where Michigan found success on the ground, running for 187 yards. It took a lot of the stress off of the true freshman quarterback.

He had some success against Washington, but against Oklahoma and Ohio State, a pair of top-10 defenses, Underwood struggled. Even as a runner. Against the Sooners and the Buckeyes, Underwood had a combined nine rushing attempts for zero yards.

Underwood may have the tools, but he has yet to show it against a team that's as talented on the defensive side of the ball as the Oklahoma Sooners are. And no, I don't consider a bowl game Texas team in the same light as a regular season defense because we know players opt out of the bowl games.

The Oklahoma Sooners' defense will be a tougher challenge than the Western Michigan one Underwood and the Wolverines faced in Week 1. Underwood completed just 54.5% of his passes for 170 yards, one touchdown, and an interception. The touchdown came on the Hail Mary that maybe shouldn't have been allowed. He also ran for 47 yards and a touchdown on nine carries, showing off the dual-threat ability that makes him a dangerous challenge.

But after facing the athletic E.J. Colson and Raymond Moore III of UTEP in Week 1, the Sooners are better prepared to slow down Underwood's rushing ability. If the Sooners play assignment-sound, disciplined football, they'll be in great shape.

articles.title: Gauff takes inspiration from Tiafoe in US Open fightback win
articles.summary: Drawing inspiration from Frances Tiafoe's rally from two sets down to reach the US Open semi-finals, Coco Gauff saved two match points in her own fightback v...
articles.body:
Drawing inspiration from Frances Tiafoe's rally from two sets down to reach the US Open semi-finals, Coco Gauff saved two match points in her own fightback victory on Wednesday.

World number four Gauff, a 22-year-old American and two-time Grand Slam winner, was on the edge of defeat in a second-set tie-breaker before ousting reigning French Open champion Mirra Andreeva 2-6, 7-6 (9/7), 6-2 to reach the US Open semi-finals.

Gauff advanced to a Thursday match at Arthur Ashe Stadium against Elena Rybakina, who beat Chinese qualifier Zheng Qinwen 3-6, 6-1, 6-4, to ensure the second-ranked Kazakh star will leap to world number one next week.

Gauff's victory was much like compatriot Tiafoe's comeback triumph Tuesday over fellow American Alex Michelsen in a dramatic five-setter.

"Sometimes you just need a little bit of inspiration, and Frances was that for me in that moment," Gauff said.

"Frances was looking -- I was watching the end of that set and it looked like he was down and out. And sometimes you just need a chance, and I think I got my chances today."

Gauff struggled in the first set and battled through four service breaks in a row for the two until a tie-break where Russian teen Andreeva had two match points but each time fired an errant forehand. Two unforced errors on the final points gave Gauff her chance and she rolled through the final set.

"I was just really determined to not lose that second set, because I felt like I worked so hard to give myself opportunities and lost them," Gauff said. "I didn't know how the third set would go, but I was just really focused on trying not to lose that second set.

"One point turned into another. Once the third set started, I felt pretty confident I was going to come out with that one."

Tiafoe, who faces American Ben Shelton in Friday's men's semis, has provided motivation beyond his never-say-die example at Flushing Meadows.

"Frances is such a light and such a joy to have on tour. Always been so nice and just hyping me up and my family up," Gauff said. "He's a special type of person and almost everybody on tour can agree that he's one of the few players who is always lighting up the room and giving respect towards us women too.

"He's a rare person in this world and in this sport."

Not that Gauff is going to tell Tiafoe any of that, adding, "I don't like to give him any credit. Hopefully he doesn't see these (remarks)."

Gauff did not message either Tiafoe or Shelton, whose early morning upset of Carlos Alcaraz was the latest-ever US Open finish.

"I feel like it's a bad luck or omen, so I usually don't like to text anyone while they're playing in a tournament," Gauff said.

Gauff, the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open winner, is excited that three black players -- herself, Tiafoe and Shelton have a chance to win at Ashe, named for a legendary 1960s black tennis pioneer. Either Tiafoe or Shelton will play for the chance to be the first US men's major winner in 23 years.

"It's so incredible. Honestly, especially on the men's side, I never thought I'd be able to have the chance to see like an all-Black semi-final between the guys in my lifetime," Gauff said.

"And to have also me in the semis, I think it's really cool."

It helps sustain Gauff's belief in herself and her game.

"Just believing is all I can do. I mean, the game may not always show up, but I can control the belief in myself," she said.

"Even if it's delusional, the more instances I keep showing up and maybe being successful in those moments, maybe that delusion will be more factual."

articles.title: Julian Edelman on Pats avoiding Mike Vrabel distraction: 'We were around murderers'
articles.summary: New England Patriots great Julian Edelman said all teams deal with distractions and the 2026 squad should deploy an "us against the world" strategy.
articles.body:
From Aaron Hernandez to "SpyGate" to "DeflateGate," Julian Edelman was no stranger to off-field distractions while with the New England Patriots .

The 2026 Patriots, coming off a Super Bowl appearance but navigating the headline-riddled offseason involving head coach Mike Vrabel , find themselves in a somewhat similar place, Edelman said.

The three-time Super Bowl champion's advice?

"You just worry about what you got on your plate that day," the Super Bowl 53 MVP said in an interview with USA TODAY Sports . "You go out and you manipulate your mind to worry about improving every single day. I mean, we've all dealt with distractions, unfortunately, in this profession. We were around murderers and big '-gates' and stuff."

Vrabel and former NFL reporter Dianna Russini were photographed at an adults-only resort in March , according to images published April 7 by Page Six. Russini ultimately resigned from her job at The Athletic, which ultimately ruled her relationship with Vrabel was inappropriate . Vrabel apologized for being a distraction in April and also said he was going to seek counseling, although he has not said anything about the topic in months .

Edelman isn't in the Patriots' locker room, so he doesn't know this team is blocking out the noise specifically. His Patriots teams of the 2010s deployed an "us against the world" mentality and encouraged the current squad to do the same.

"If you have a mentally tough group of men who can literally focus on 'what (do) we have to do today to improve?'" said Edelman, who spoke to USA TODAY on behalf of Sam Adams, which is launching a beer named after him. "That's how you get your results."

articles.title: Fantasy Baseball Steals Report: Henry Bolte in on fire, Pete Crow-Armstrong will not stop
articles.summary: Who is stealing bases, who isn't, why, and how?
articles.body:
Welcome to the steals report! I will be here every Wednesday to go over important stolen base trends so you can find more speed for your fantasy teams.

Stealing a base is as much about the opposing pitcher and catcher as it is the actual base runner themself. So, being able to spot which teams and pitchers specifically are being run on most frequently will help you to figure out who can swipe some bags over the next week.

Understanding who's stealing bases is even more important this time of year because with so much of the season already gone, it's difficult to find ways to rise up in most categories. Yet, steals often have the least volume of all the categories, so the breadth isn't as wide and a few shrewd moves can help you earn a lot of roto points.

Before we get to this week's important trends, here is the stolen base leaderboard on the season so far.

Eric Samulski breaks down recent pitching changes for 11 different starting pitchers

There have been very few changes to this leaderboard over the past few weeks. So, I'm introducing a new, more timely one right here.

Just as Jazz Chisholm Jr. was finally breaking out of his season-long slump, he landed on the injured list with a sprained right thumb. Anthony Volpe will come up to take his roster spot.

Henry Bolte is on a heater. Along with those five stolen bases over the past week, he went 10-for-25 with three home runs and a 1.345 OPS. He has unbelievable tools and while it's taken him a bit to acclimate to the big league game, it seems like he's turned the corner and needs to be rostered in every single league.

Before swiping three bags in his last four games, Sal Stewart stole just one in the 70 games prior.

It's nice to see that aggressiveness from Oneil Cruz on the basepaths now that he's been off the injured list for a few weeks.

While a calf injury and the Mets falling out of contention early has likely caused Juan Soto to be less aggressive on the base paths, not even cracking 10 stolen bases this season is a disappointment.

The Cardinals allowed the most stolen bases over the past week with 10 across seven games.

Three of those came in one of the two games that Iván Herrera started at catcher. He was replaced for a pinch-runner in the other.

Herrera has appeared on this column a few times this season because he's a poor defensive player and has only caught two of 45 would-be base stealers all season. That 4% caught stealing rate is worst in the league among all players who've caught at least 200 innings.To make matters worse, that's only come in 50 starts behind the plate.

Otherwise, the Cardinals promoted Leo Bernal last week when the rosters expanded and he may be their catcher of the future. A switch-hitter with real power from each side of the plate, Bernal had 16 home runs, nine stolen bases, and a 115 wRC+ through 101 games at Triple-A this season as a 22-year-old with a strong underlying profile to match. He's also started nine games in a row since being called up.

He figures to be a solid offensive contributor in the near-term with potential for much more in the future, but leaves a bit to be desired on the defensive side. Especially compared to Pedro Pagés , who seems to be the third catcher on the Cardinals depth chart now. That change suddenly makes the Cardinals one of the best teams to stream stolen bases against.

They're matched up with the White Sox and Giants over the next week. So, Tristan Peters , Sam Antonacci , Jonah Cox , Jung-Hoo Lee , and Osleivis Basabe are solid options if you're seeking speed.

A few weeks ago, Pete Crow-Armstong stole his 30th base to join the 30-30 club for the second consecutive season. He's since pushed forward by clearing 40 home runs and is approaching 40 stolen bases as he marches towards his first MVP award.

CJ Abrams is on pace to go 30-30 as well with 30 home runs and 28 stolen bases entering play on Wednesday. Besides them, Elly De La Cruz could get there too with 25 home runs and stolen bases apiece, but it would take some late season heroics for any other player to reach that milestone.

When the league altered the rules to make bases easier to steal ahead of the 2023 season, 30-30 seasons sky-rocketed. In the three full seasons before the change, there were only three players who went 30-30: Christian Yelich and Ronald Acuña Jr. in 2019 and Cedric Mullins in 2021.

Between 2023 and 2025, it happened 14 times. That included some extremes like Acuña swiping 73, Shohei Ohtani going 50-50, and Juan Soto beating his former career-best in steals by 26 bags.

That trend seems to have stopped this season as stolen bases have dried up a tad. Maybe teams are more prepared to control the run game or there's more risk-averse behavior going on from a base running perspective. Either way, it's a break from what we thought was the new norm.

articles.title: Elly De La Cruz Sets A New Record With 102 MPH Throw To Home Plate
articles.summary: Elly De La Cruz put on a show at Dodger Stadium on Tuesday night, hitting a home run in his fourth straight game and throwing a ball 102 mph to cut down a ru...
articles.body:
On Tuesday night in Los Angeles , Cincinnati Reds ' shortstop Elly De La Cruz hit a home run in his fourth consecutive game. His latest came in the top of third inning, with Dane Myers on first base. De La Cruz was ready for Tarik Skubal 's first-pitch change-up and smashed it 109.4 mph and 444-feet into the left field bleachers. That blast tied the game at two. Skubal only gave up two more hits the rest of the way, and the Dodgers won the game 3-2.

But the score could have been – maybe should have been – 4-2 if not for De La Cruz's heroics on the field. In the bottom half that same third inning, Dodger left field Teoscar Hernández hit a low line drive to center field. Myers dove forward in an attempt to make an acrobatic catch, but instead watched the ball roll all the way to the wall.

Hernández got on his horse and tried to turn a certain triple into his first inside-the-park home run in his professional career. Left fielder JJ Bleday hustled over and picked the ball up on the warning track and threw it back towards the infield. That is where De La Cruz was waiting. Cruz caught the ball in a perfect position to throw to the plate. And that is when he unleased a 102 mph fastball to catcher Jose Trevino from nearly 200 feet away. Truth be told, the ball was a little low and offline, but Trevino was easily able to catch it on a short hop on the right side of the plate and slide over to put an easy tag on Hernández, who was out by so much that didn't even try to make it all the way home.

It is hard to say with certainty if even an average throw would have retired Hernández at the plate, but we don't have to do that analysis.

According to Savant , De La Cruz's arm strength is in the 91 st percentile. It has been his calling card since he came into the league in 2023. And he called on that card Tuesday night in a way that no one ever has. The throw to retire Hernández was the hardest tracked assist by an infielder in the entire Statcast era, which goes back to 2015. In fact, according to MLB.com , Elly broke his own record "four times over."

Prior to Tuesday night, here is a sampling of some of Elly's other lasers, which happen to be the hardest-tracked assists by an infielder in the Statcast era:

1 st (tie): Elly De La Cruz: 99.8 mph, 8/8/2026 1 st (tie): Elly De La Cruz: 99.8 mph, 7/20/2023 2 nd : Elly De La Cruz: 99.7 mph, 8/27/2023 3 rd : Elly De La Cruz: 99.2 mph, 8/19/2026

However, even at 102 mph, he still trails Brenton Doyle , who unfurled a ball at 105.7 mph in 2023 to keep a runner from scoring on a potential sacrifice fly.

And Doyle was just slightly faster than Aaron Hicks , who let loose with a 105.5 mph rocket in 2016 to complete a double play with Danny Valencia trying to score from third base.

This season De La Cruz is slashing .283/.362/.506, which is a 5.0 bWAR season. But don't let the gaudy offensive stats fool you – that encompasses his 0.2 dWAR and he has a .971 fielding percentage. He is 12 th in MLB in Outs Above Average with 7 ( Bobby Witt Jr. leads with 23).

With the bat – from either side of the plate – with the glove, and especially with his arm, what 48,000 fans saw last night at Dodger Stadium was the full Elly De La Cruz experience.
